releases.name: reeve 0.2.7
releases.body:
**Free-pool cooldowns now escalate instead of resetting.** A free model that
keeps failing used to re-enter a fixed 600 s cooldown and — worse — when a
cooldown expired the whole record was deleted, handing the model a fresh
failure budget. A persistently rate-limited upstream (429 all day) therefore
burned 3 doomed attempts every ~10 minutes, forever (observed: two dead models
burned 12 attempts in 40 minutes). Now each model's consecutive-offense count
is remembered when a cooldown expires (the entry stays, `fails` resets, one
probe attempt is allowed); failing again re-enters cooldown at
`failure_cooldown_seconds × 2^(offenses−1)`, capped by the new
`free.cooldown_cap_seconds` (default 86400). One successful attempt clears the
record entirely, so a recovered upstream returns to the base cooldown. The
`/gate/free` runtime snapshot reports `offenses` per cooling ref so the panel
can show "how many times has this model re-entered cooldown". Config gains
`free.cooldown_cap_seconds` (60–604800); everything else is unchanged.
Plugin-only release — the panel extension is untouched.

releases.name: reeve 0.2.6
releases.body:
**Tier metadata now follows the chain — no manual upkeep.** The composer's
model popover used to show dashes for cost and release date, and (worse) a
fabricated `1M` context on `reeve/free`. GATE now exposes
`GET /gate/model-meta`: per-tier cost (input/output/cache read+write),
context/output limits, and release date, computed from the **first target of
the chain each tier maps to** — so editing a chain in the panel updates the
popover data too (GATE hot-reloads; the plugin refreshes on its existing
state poll and calls `provider.reload()` when the data changes, on engines
that expose it — older engines degrade to "next rebuild/restart"). The data
source is the models.dev payload GATE already fetches (6h TTL, zero new
outbound traffic); provider names are resolved through three levels
(exact key → `canonical_model_id` → globally unique model id). Anything the
catalog does not know is **omitted entirely** rather than guessed — the free
pool's popular models have no entries today, so `reeve/free` cost is $0 (free
by definition) with context falling back to the new `free.context_floor`
(default 131072), which stops the engine from letting sessions grow past what
the pool can actually serve. `buildTierModel` ships the same numbers as
cold-start fallback (`STATIC_TIER_META`); values written by hand under
`providers.reeve.models.*` in opencode.jsonc are never touched.

releases.name: reeve 0.2.5
releases.body:
**New tier `reeve/free`: the free-pool-only chain.** `default-fallback.json`
gains a `free-only` chain whose only target is `@free`, and `chain_for_model`
maps the new fifth tier `reeve/free` to it. The guarantee is structural: the
chain has no paid candidates, so when the free pool is disabled, empty, or every
candidate fails, the request ends in a 502 — it never falls through to a paid
target. Three new free-pool tests pin the success path (free candidates only,
zero paid upstream calls), the exhausted path (502, zero paid calls), and the
pool-disabled path (empty plan 502 with no upstream request). A unit test now
pins the bundled mapping to exactly the five tier keys.

**Panel (extension 0.1.15).** The `chain_for_model` editor shows a row for
`reeve/free`; the `free-only` chain card renders like any chain (its `@free`
row shows「免费模型池」). New audit item 45 pins the dedicated-chain card.

**Upgrade note.** The user-level `fallback.jsonc` replaces the bundled default
 wholesale (no per-key merge). Machines that already have one must add the two
keys by hand — `chains["free-only"] = { "targets": ["@free"] }` and
`chain_for_model["reeve/free"] = "free-only"` — or selecting `reeve/free`
returns 404.
